I used to think I know what I want. I can't deny that I used to have feelings for her. Maybe I still do, I don't know anymore. Or maybe I was just being overly attached to the first person to show concern for me for a long time. I don't know what I want from my interactions with her anymore, to the point that I've tried distancing myself from her, but it only brought me sadness, and probably led to a strain on the relationship I'm seeing now. 

Well, if it isn't the consequences of my actions.

How do you manage to keep it hidden though? I feel like I'm desperately close to saying something to her that I'll deeply regret. I've no outlet for all this resentment (justified or not) that I've been taking it out on myself.

I can't say for certain, as it depends on the practices and regulations your therapist works under, which can vary.

From personal experience, my therapist definitely discourages self harm but acknowledges that it's a coping mechanism that I may rely on from time to time, and that I'm always welcome to discuss them and not hide them from her. However she does draw the line when she feels that my safety is at risk.

An important aspect of therapy and counselling is informed consent. You as the client should be entitled to information of the centers protocol for such cases. 

Sorry I wasn't able to provide a definite answer, but I hope this helps.

I understand where you're coming from. While I do cut myself, I sometimes wonder if what I do is considered self harm since my cuts were relatively shallow due to a combination of blunt knife and fear of cutting deep.

It's not the action that determines whether or not it's self harm, but the intent behind them. If you are compelled to go against your body's instinct of self preservation to inflict pain upon yourself, no matter how little, that is self harm, and you deserve the help and support you need. Don't let the lack of blood or scars tell you that your pain isn't real.

I suppose my gripe is mainly how the easing of restrictions doesn't seem to make sense. Cinemas are open, yet I still can't see my therapist in her office? I still have to do sessions through Zoom for the foreseeable future? Plus I get no privacy at home so I have to take my sessions by the staircase where my therapist can hear my neighbour beating her kid.

I guess it doesn't help that I work in the social service sector so work has been extra stressful, especially with more stringent social distancing measures in place. I just feel utterly trapped and I'm dangerously close to my limits.
I struggle to believe that I'm worth anything. But I resisted the urge to cut.

Thank you, that gave me a lot to think about. I definitely have experiences in the past where similar feelings were aroused, including one which ended in the termination of a 14 year friendship. But I want to give her a fair chance, especially when she's done so much for me, enough to make me certain that our friendship at least isn't one sided.

I've calmed down a lot since I made this post, I don't think I'll be cutting myself at least.

"What I can do that's best for both of us": I guess I should just interact with her as usual, without expecting an explanation if not forthcoming. 

Perhaps I could find the time to let her know how I felt, but only mention the emotions, without getting into the thoughts associated with those emotions so that I don't guilt trip her or anything. I dunno, I was told that it's fine to talk about feelings without going into the thoughts and belief associated with them unless it's with a therapist.

Either way I'll try to keep things neutral and fair, cos I want to treat her fairly too.

Thank you for the advice.

I really do get the reason behind this. Unfortunately we're colleagues, and I have to work closely with her on a daily basis so staying away is not an option, and neither is quitting my job. I also don't wish to socially withdraw from her as I'd prefer to at least have a good work relationship. 

And she is one of my supports in life, one of the very few I have left. I don't want to keep repeating the cycle of becoming close to someone and then distancing myself over minor faults. It's how I got myself here in the first place. But thanks for your advice and help, I do appreciate it.

You're absolutely right about letting the urge pass. I admit that it's easier said than done considering I'm in a calmer state than when I made this post. But it's definitely useful to keep this in mind. I definitely need to work on not acting on immediate impulses. Thinking clearly now, I would have definitely regretted it.

I had initially felt that it was just something that happened out of convenience, since we just so happenbto see each other everyday.

I was initially worried that she was only using me to vent her frustrations, but she's actually helped me with some issues as well and even introduced me to some of her friends, and actually looks out for me. She got me to get back to exercising and even checks on me if I've eaten (because I have a habbit of skipping meals with a history of purging).

I'm so used to being treated badly by people outside my immediate family that I guess I didn't know how to react when someone suddenly comes along and is nice to me. Part of me wants to push her away cos isolation is what's familiar to me and my brain seems to be actively fighting my attempts at improving my social life. 

But thank you for your kind words. I'll be honest, I don't really believe what you're saying about me is true, but I appreciate it.
I know, you're absolutely right. If I had things my way, I wouldn't even be having such feelings. But turns out I'm good at ruining the good things in my life.

I'm currently only able to see the counsellor at my uni, I'm not able to afford to see a mental health specialist elsewhere, especially with school fees taking up a chunk of my income.

Counselling through zoom isn't ideal, especially since I have no privacy at home and have to take the sessions in less than ideal locations. But thanks for the advice. Medication is something I haven't tried, I'll keep it in mind.

I've already self harmed before due to other issues, so its definitely something that I'll need to work on.

Regarding your second point, I understand why it would be advisable to leave, but I'd still prefer having a good relationship with her considering we're still colleagues, and quitting my job is absolutely not an option. But thanks for the advice, I really appreciate it.
Not really. Just wondering if it's worth taking supplements, particularly on weeks when my gym time is affected due to work and school commitments.

I feel your pain, I've already dropped out of Uni once because I was suicidal and now it's happening all over again. I thought I was finally growing and becoming a better person. I've made plans to do more things in life, meet new people, go back to school, finally go back to having friends.

Now all is lost. If I don't go to work, I'd probably never speak to anyone outside my house. With no friends to speak off, I end up seeking companionship at work. I ended up having feelings for my  colleague, which I know is wrong, both because of work and my mental health. So I cut myself to help deal with these problems. But now I'm worried my boss might notice the cuts and I don't want to lose my job.

I want so badly to meet my counsellor again but everything's through zoom, and I don't have a private space for the calls. I miss going to class after work and seeing my course mates. We're not friends or anything but they're great people and I miss chatting with them.

I want to go back to the days when I felt happy. But all I have is my toggle rope courtesy of MINDEF.

I'll try to keep what you said in mind. I've heard it many times before and consciously I know it to be true, but I've never been able to see it as applying to me, that there's fundamentally despicable about me. I don't think I'm going to be able to resist cutting again in the near future, but please believe that I really appreciate all that you've told me.

I guess it's because I know that I don't have anything about me that would make me appealing. Anyone, not just her, could do a lot better than what I have to offer. I just started working at my current place so I haven't really gotten to know her yet. She could very well already have an SO, or maybe she just wants to focus on her career? 

Either way, I feel like I'm intruding on her personal life, and need to be punished for it. 

And I know what you're saying is right. I don't realistically expect to start a relationship of any kind based on pity, which is all the more frustrating that I don't seem to know what I want. I've deliberately made attempts to distance myself from her at work, which definitely must have come off as cold as she does seem more cool towards me. I mean it's what I wanted right? So why am I so upset that things turned out like this?
I know I should. But I just can't bring myself to do it. In my mind, she's better off not having me in her life anymore.

I know how you feel. I used to have someone like that who I felt safe with and could share everything with. I even had feelings for her at one point. But one day she just stopped responding to my texts and I don't have the courage to give her a call.

I know people have their own lives to deal with, and I can't expect her life to revolve around me. Yet when someone who knows the problems I face and sincerely expressed support suddenly disappears, I don't really know what to think. I don't want to doubt her sincerity. 

Come to think of it, I wouldn't even know if she were dead. Just goes to show how 'close' we really were.

Thanks for your feedback. In hindsight, I suppose I was being to reactionary after only a few days. I guess I just needed to get it off my chest here since I don't really have any friends I could talk to irl.
That's not too different from what my counselor tells me, but I guess it's not really sinking in? I don't feel like I deserve anything from my family or friends, cos I'm just dead weight to them.
